settings.title: Looking for more answers?
settings.q1_question: Why do you recommend 2 bottles minimum?
settings.q1_answer:
Our 312-woman clinical panel saw the shift at week 7–8. Not week 3. Not week 4.

The flush loop that keeps your face reactive doesn't unwind in 30 days. It needs 56 days for the alarm to stop firing, the nerves to reset, and the barrier to fully rebuild — and closer to 84 days for that new baseline to hold on its own.

One bottle tests whether your skin tolerates the formula. Two bottles tests whether it works. Three bottles is where the panel said the shift stabilizes.

If it doesn't shift for you — every bottle, even the half-used ones, is refunded within 60 days. One email. No forms. That's why the guarantee is 60 days, not 30.
settings.q2_question: Will this actually work if nothing else has?
settings.q2_answer:
A fair question given what you've probably tried already.

Most rosacea products target one mechanism — either the immune alarm, or the vessels, or the barrier. That's why single-active serums plateau. Your face has five things misfiring at once, and treating one of them just lets the other four keep running the loop.

The Reset Complex targets the five simultaneously — that's the mechanical difference. It's why our panel saw shifts in cases where prescriptions, IPL, and every “sensitive skin” line had failed.

That said, we're honest about one thing: 4 out of 100 women in our panel saw no change at all. If you're in that 4 out of 100, the 60-day refund is why.
settings.q3_question: Is Rosalia safe if I'm pregnant or nursing?
settings.q3_answer:
Yes. Every active in Rosalia was chosen with pregnancy- and nursing-compatibility in mind, using standard OB and lactation references.

Azelaic Acid — one of our four actives — is specifically recommended by dermatologists during pregnancy for exactly the kind of hormonal flushing that shows up postpartum.

We still recommend confirming with your OB or lactation consultant before starting anything new — every body is different, and we're not your doctor. But we built the formula so you wouldn't have to wait until you're done nursing to start.
settings.d1_body:
Four clinically-supported actives, each at the dose reactive skin can actually tolerate.

Azelaic Acid 10%, Centella Asiatica 4%, Colloidal Oat 1% + Panthenol (B5) 5%, Licochalcone A 0.4%. Chosen because more isn't better when your skin is already on edge. The fifth lever isn't an ingredient — it's what your face does when the first four stop interfering.

What we left out on purpose: essential oils, fragrance, alcohol, menthol, niacinamide (one of the most common inducers of flushing in reactive skin), retinoids.
settings.d2_body:
Rosacea isn't one thing misfiring — it's five systems firing at once: the alarm (immune overreaction), the nerves (heat/stress hypersensitivity), the door (barrier leak that feeds the alarm), the wall (vessels that stay dilated), and the loop that keeps them all going.

The Reset Complex targets four of the five with actives. The fifth (the loop) unwinds on its own once the first four stop interfering. That's why single-active serums plateau — they fix one, the other four keep the loop running.

Full mechanism in the “Rosacea was never one problem” section below.
settings.d3_body:
Morning and evening, on clean dry skin, before your moisturizer.

01 · Dispense
3–4 drops from the dropper. Enough for the full face.
02 · Apply
Press gently into cheeks, nose, forehead. Let it absorb for 60 seconds.
03 · Continue
Follow with moisturizer. The serum works underneath.

Compatible with most routines. The only caution: avoid high-concentration acids (AHA/BHA above 5%) in the same application.

settings.lead: Most serums are built for skin that already behaves. Rosalia was built for skin that doesn't.

settings.quote: I keep forgetting to check my face.
settings.comment: Ok so the 4pm thing. My cheeks would start burning around then pretty much every day at work and I'd go sit in the bathroom for ten minutes until it passed. I realised last week I hadn't done that in a while. I couldn't tell you when it stopped, which is kind of the strange part — you don't notice the day it happens.
settings.name: Camille

settings.quote: Down to tinted moisturiser most days.
settings.comment:
I used to put on two pumps of full coverage before leaving the house. Now it's tinted moisturiser, and some days nothing. My skin isn't perfect, I still go red after a hot shower or a glass of wine, but it's not the first thing I see in the mirror anymore.

Took about six weeks before I noticed much, so don't panic if week two feels like nothing is happening.
settings.name: Emily

settings.quote: It doesn't sting. That's why I kept going.
settings.comment:
Honestly I bought this half expecting to return it. Everything stings. This one didn't, first time in years, so I stuck with it. Six weeks in and the redness is calmer, especially around my nose.

Taking a star off for the dropper — it dribbles down the side of the bottle every time. Small thing but it bugs me.
settings.name: Sarah

settings.quote: I stopped scheduling around my face.
settings.comment: For years I avoided afternoon meetings because I knew what my face would look like by then. I don't really think about that now. It still happens sometimes, usually when I'm stressed or it's warm out, but it's mild and it fades in a few minutes instead of sticking around all evening.
settings.name: Julie

settings.quote: My dermatologist asked what I'd changed.
settings.comment:
Went in for a routine check and she stopped halfway through and asked what I was using. I told her it was just this, and she wrote the name down.

I've been on and off prescriptions since my twenties. Nothing has held like this has.
settings.name: Sophie

settings.quote: the bumps are what actually changed
settings.comment:
the redness got better but honestly the bumps are the thing that changed for me. i had them along my jaw and chin constantly, like a whole cluster. now there's maybe one or two.

wish it was a bit cheaper tbh. but i've repurchased twice so.
settings.name: Ana

settings.question: How is this different from prescriptions?
settings.answer: Prescriptions typically target one pathway. The Reset Complex addresses five simultaneously. Not a replacement — what you reach for when prescriptions plateau.

settings.question: When will I see results?
settings.answer: Our 312-woman panel saw the shift at week 7–8. Full effect stabilizes around week 10–12. Not overnight — a systematic reset that builds.

settings.question: Can I use with my existing routine?
settings.answer: Yes. Apply on clean skin before moisturizer. Compatible with most routines. Only caution: avoid high-concentration acids (AHA/BHA above 5%) in the same application.

settings.question: What if it doesn't work?
settings.answer: Email us. Within 60 days, any reason, full refund to your account within 24 hours. No forms. No return shipping. No questions.

settings.question: I've tried everything. Why would this be different?
settings.answer: Because everything you've tried targets one thing. One ingredient, one pathway, one hope. Rosacea has five simultaneous dysfunctions. The Reset Complex is the first formula designed to address all five at once. That's not marketing — that's why single-active serums always plateau.

settings.question: Will this make my skin purge or get worse first?
settings.answer: No. There is no purging phase. The formula contains zero actives known to cause purging (no retinoids, no high-dose acids). If anything, the first thing you'll notice is that your skin stops stinging when you apply it. That's the barrier beginning to rebuild.

settings.question: Is this safe during perimenopause / menopause?
settings.answer: Yes. Hormonal flushing is one of the specific patterns the Reset Complex was designed for. Lever 02 (The Nerves) and Lever 04 (The Wall) directly address the vascular instability that worsens during hormonal transitions. Several of our longest-term users are perimenopausal women.
